evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 釋義; 零 record A04475
evidence.text: The entry reports the Great Xu Shuowen text as 餘雨也。从雨，令聲 and the Duan Yucai edition as 徐雨也。从雨，霝聲. It cites the Shijing phrase 我來自東，零雨其濛 and records senses for slow rain, falling, withering, tears, scattered or residual amounts, and numeric zero. These dictionary examples do not establish a dated sequence between the senses.
evidence.title: A04475 零 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 零 as 雨 semantic plus 令 phonetic and glosses its early sense as rain, snow, frost, or dew falling. It cites 靈雨既零 with Mao commentary 零，落也, then examples for withering, death or old age, tears, a remainder, and modern zero. The page does not date these cited compositions or surviving witnesses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 零

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 甲骨文解說; 霝 entry
evidence.text: The entry reports oracle-bone and bronze forms and uses for 霝, but says proposed explanations of its graph (rain plus two or three 口, among others) lack strong evidence and that its original graph meaning remains unresolved. This is evidence about 霝, not proof that 零 itself occurs in oracle-bone inscriptions.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 雨部 / 霝

evidence.text: The supplied exact local Baxter–Sagart rows report 零 líng, MC leng, OC *[r]ˤiŋ (gloss ‘fall of rain’); 令 includes 脊令 ‘water bird’ líng, MC leng, OC *[r]ˤiŋ, plus ‘send’ *riŋ and ‘issue a command’ *riŋ-s. 雨 has rain *C.ɢʷ(r)aʔ and verbal rain *[ɢ]ʷ(r)aʔ-s. evidence.source: 漢語“〇”概念的不同形式和相关结构, Hanspub PDF
evidence.text: This secondary study distinguishes the zero-placeholder sign 〇 from the character 零. It reports 零 as a placeholder in Qin Jiushao’s 1247 Shushu jiuzhang and connects this use to the ‘remainder’ sense, while arguing that 零 as a numeral for zero came later. It separately reports 〇 as a positional placeholder in the 1180 Daming li. The accessible primary-text pages checked here did not independently verify the cited 零 passage, so 1247 is a reported earliest example, not independently confirmed in this research.
evidence.title: 汉语“〇”概念的不同形式和相关结构

evidence.source: 識典古籍, digitized text of 數書九章
evidence.field: 卷第一大衍類; 收數者 passage
evidence.text: The opened text identifies Qin Jiushao as author and gives the passage ‘收数者，乃命尾位分厘作单零，以进所问之数’. This shows 零 in a fractional/remainder-related technical context in the displayed text. The page does not establish the work’s manuscript witness or independently show that this phrase is a zero-placeholder use.

gaps: No directly inspected oracle-bone or bronze attestation of 零 was found. The dossier claim that oracle-bone 零 depicts raindrops is unsupported by the inspected pages and should not be repeated.

The traditional 雨 + 令 phonosemantic analysis is documented by Shuowen tradition and modern dictionaries. The alternative Duan-edition account says 霝聲; no inspected source establishes whether that disagreement is textual transmission, graphic analysis, or corruption.

Local Baxter–Sagart rows provide 零 *[r]ˤiŋ / MC leng and one 令 bird reading with the same values, alongside other distinct 令 readings. The external PDF failed to open, so do not represent these exact local rows as independently fetched external evidence. The local rows do not uniquely determine which historical 令 reading is intended in 零.

Current readings in supplied local rows are 零 líng, 令 lìng, 雨 yǔ, and 霝 líng. Official Unicode character records for 零 and 令 failed to open in the actual attempts; the 霝 and 雨 records were not attempted. No full externally verified reading array is available for every component.

The Shijing examples establish a literary rain/falling use in the cited textual tradition, but composition dates and earliest surviving witnesses were not established. Later dictionaries cite distinct extensions for falling, withering, tears, remnants, and zero without dating a complete semantic sequence.

A secondary study reports 零 as a placeholder in Qin Jiushao’s 1247 text and separates it from the earlier circular placeholder 〇. The opened digitized primary text contains 零 in a technical fractional/remainder passage but does not, in the inspected lines, independently verify the placeholder claim. Li Ye’s 1248 use of 零 was not established.

The CUHK discussion of oracle-bone and bronze glyphs concerns 霝. Its account says the original graph interpretation remains unresolved; this does not establish the depicted object/name or pronunciation of any object borrowed as a whole graph. No whole-graph borrowing analysis for 零 was found.
The seal-script candidate is a modern redraw; no ancient 零 image or dated inscription was verified. No recurring-source bulk reuse terms were investigated, so no extract recommendation is made.
